subject: history
title: End of the Cold War: Interpretations
welcome_lead: Today you'll stretch — why did the Cold War end and who deserves the credit?
meta_desc: GCSE History stretch — Gorbachev, Reagan, fall of the Berlin Wall and interpretations of the Cold War's end.
final_note: You can now weigh different interpretations of why the Cold War ended.

concepts.def: 1979-89 Soviet war that drained the USSR
Gorbachev's policy of restructuring the economy
Polish trade union that challenged communist rule
9 Nov 1989 — symbolic end of the divided Europe

walkthroughs.body_html:
By the 1980s the Soviet economy was stagnant.

The Afghanistan war (1979-89) cost lives and money. President Reagan pushed an arms build-up the USSR could not match.

From 1985 Mikhail Gorbachev launched glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring).

He also signalled he would not crush reform in Eastern Europe. In Poland, the Solidarity movement won elections in 1989.

On 9 November 1989 the Berlin Wall fell. By Christmas 1991 the USSR was dissolved.

Some historians credit Reagan's pressure. Others credit Gorbachev's choices. Others highlight the courage of ordinary people in Berlin, Prague and Warsaw. All three have evidence — strong answers weigh them together.

numericals.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
